gitUpdate.notes: autoUpdate: true -> after boot, bot silently checks the public GitHub repo at url every checkIntervalMinutes and silently downloads a newer version in the background (never blocks boot/login). Once downloaded it DMs every adminBot ID: react with checkmark on that message, or send the update command, to apply it (applies + restarts). false -> disabled. cmdUpdate: true -> updates also overwrite modules/cmds (your commands); set to false to always skip modules/cmds during an update, so your local/custom commands are never touched, only the core bot code updates. branch: leave empty to auto-detect the repo default branch. checkIntervalMinutes: how often (minutes) to check in the background, minimum 5. protectedPaths: the full list of files/folders (relative to project root) that are NEVER overwritten by an update - this is shown here so you can see exactly what's excluded; edit with care, removing an entry means that file/folder CAN be overwritten by an update. protect: extra files/folders you want to add to that exclusion list, without having to touch protectedPaths.

notesLanguage: change to your language with ISO 639-1 code, available languages: vi (Vietnamese), en (English)

database.notes: (1) type selects 'json' or 'sqlite' or 'mongodb'. If you choose mongodb, enter uri connect mongodb in the uriMongodb section, instructions to get uri connect mongodb at: https://youtu.be/z1f9urHW5xY. I recommend using 'mongodb' or 'sqlite', json is not recommended because it is not stable. (2) when you set autoSyncWhenStart to true, the bot will automatically synchronize the data in the database when starting the bot, this will make the bot start slower. (3) when you set autoRefreshThreadInfoFirstTime to true, the bot will automatically refresh the thread information when get first message from the thread since starting the bot

autoUptime.notes: the value of timeInterval is seconds, url is the url you want to send the request to (automatically detected for hosting glitch or replit)

notiWhenListenMqttError.notes: This is the message when the bot is listening to the mqtt server and the mqtt server stops working due to account problems such as: locked acc, blocked due to spam,... bot will automatically send notifications to parts of your settings. You must change enable to true to use this feature. See bot/login/handlerWhenListenHasError.js file for details on how it works

telegram.note: Can send notifications to many chatId, separate by comma or space, example: "123456789 987654321" (without backslash)

discordHook.note: Can send notifications to many webhookUrl, separate by comma or space, example: "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/123456789/123456789 https://discord.com/api/webhooks/987654321/987654321" (without backslash)

e2ee.notes: enable: true/false turns Facebook E2EE (Labyrinth) chat support on or off for every Fca module (send/unsend/react/typing/edit + the MQTT E2EE bridge in listenMqtt). Since the bridge connects once when the bot starts listening, changing 'enable' requires a bot restart to take effect. saveType: 'path' persists the E2EE device key pair to devicePath so the same encrypted-chat device is reused across restarts (recommended - avoids Facebook flagging a new device every boot); 'memory' keeps the keys in RAM only and registers a fresh device every restart. deviceData: leave null unless you are manually restoring exported device keys.
